speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. To begin our evaluation of your acute diarrhea, please describe exactly what your symptoms are, how long they have been lasting, and if you have experienced any fever or blood in your stool.

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Clostridioides difficile infection. The patient is a 58-year-old female with a clear history of recent levofloxacin use for pneumonia, presenting with acute watery diarrhea (≥9 episodes/24h) and cramping, which is the classic clinical presentation for C. diff colitis.
